Fitting ||(uv||)-CS-theory to helium with the new correction Ansatz

Marimo port of parameter_adjustment.ipynb / Helium_Parameters.ipynb: the base Mie potential (sigma, epsilon_k, rep, att) stays fixed at the Thijs-optimized values, and only the Feynman-Hibbs-1 correction coefficients c_sigma, c_epsilon_k, c_rep (5 slots each, ||(\xi_0 .. \xi_4||)) are fit.

Effective coefficients

||[ \frac{\sigma^{\text{eff}}}{\sigma} = \frac{1 + \xi_0 C_0(\sigma)\,D^{*} + \xi_1 C_1(\sigma)\,D^{*2} + \xi_3 D^{*2}} {1 + \xi_2 C_2(\sigma)\,D^{*} + \xi_4 D^{*2}} \qquad \frac{\varepsilon^{\text{eff}}}{\varepsilon} = \frac{1 + \xi_0 C_0(\varepsilon)\,D^{*} + \xi_1 C_1(\varepsilon)\,D^{*2} + \xi_3 D^{*2}} {1 + \xi_2 C_2(\varepsilon)\,D^{*} + \xi_4 D^{*2}} ||]||[ \frac{\nu^{\text{eff}}}{\nu} = \frac{1 + \xi_0 C_0(\nu)\,D^{*} + \xi_1 C_1(\nu)\,D^{*2} + \xi_2 C_2(\nu)\,D^{*3}} {1 + \xi_3 C_3(\nu)\,D^{*} + \xi_4 C_4(\nu)\,D^{*2}} ||]with ||(D^* = \hbar^2/(12 k_B T m \sigma^2)||). Earlier versions of this notebook fixed ||(\xi_0=\xi_2=1||) per property (9 free parameters total), following parameter_adjustment.ipynb's eos_from_parameters layout. That turned out to be less expressive than Thijs's own baseline in the directions that matter: Thijs fits ||(\xi_0,\xi_1,\xi_2||) freely for every property (all three carry a genuine ||(C_i(m)||) prefactor, so they're well-scaled and directly comparable to Thijs's values like c_sigma = [4.15, 17.13, 4.65, ...]), while pinning them at 1 left only ||(\xi_1||) as a real degree of freedom per property — ||(\xi_3,\xi_4||) (the bare ||(D^{*2}||) terms with no ||(C_i(m)||) prefactor) need values of order 10-100 just to matter and are regularized toward 0 below anyway (see further down). So fixing ||(\xi_0=\xi_2=1||) threw away exactly the freedom Thijs relies on. All 15 slots are now free (||(\xi_0..\xi_4||) for each of c_sigma, c_epsilon_k, c_rep) — a strict superset of Thijs's parameterization, so the fit can only match or beat it, never do worse from capacity alone. parameter_adjustment.ipynb's cost only matched vapor pressure and its least_squares call returned the initial guess unchanged (popt.x == p0) — a sign the objective wasn't actually constraining the fit. This notebook follows fit_saft_vrcs_marimo.py's more robust recipe instead: liquid and vapor density (liquid weighted 2x) + vapor pressure along the sub-critical VLE curve, density along the isotherms, and the critical point, each residual group scaled by ||(1/\sqrt{n_\mathrm{group}}||) so no single group's size dominates or vanishes in the sum of squares. (Vapor density used to be purely emergent — never in the objective — which is likely why it was the weakest metric against NIST; it's now fit directly.)

Helium configuration

  • base: fixed Mie potential (sigma, epsilon_k, rep, att=6), the Thijs-optimized values also used as the uvcs baseline's base.
  • vrqmie: SAFT-VRQ-Mie baseline (Aasen et al., FH order 1).
  • uvcs: Thijs's ||(uv||)-CS-theory fit (3-slot c_sigma/c_epsilon_k, padded to 5 with zeros for the effective-parameter formulas below).
  • t_min: low-temperature VLE cutoff below which the phase-equilibrium solver becomes unreliable.
  • pc_extrap_n: number of highest-temperature rows of the unfiltered VLE table used to linearly extrapolate p_c to tc (NIST's table stops just short of Tc).
Reference data (NIST) and baseline models

Effective-parameter formulas

Ported 1:1 from crates/feos/src/uvcs/corresponding_states.rs (effective_sigma/effective_epsilon_k/effective_repulsive_exponent_ratio — same polynomial constants, same rational-function form, same ||(D^*||) prefactor), so both the fit's low-||(D^*||) anchor below and the evaluation plot further down re-evaluate the existing Rust formulas rather than approximating them.

||(uv||)-CS fit with the new Ansatz

eos_from_parameters builds the 5-slot c_sigma/c_epsilon_k/c_rep vectors directly from the 15 free coefficients (pars[0:5], pars[5:10], pars[10:15]) — all slots free, matching Thijs's own parameterization plus the two new bare-||(D^{*2}||) slots per property. cost returns the concatenated relative-residual vector that least_squares minimizes.

Each deviation group (liquid density, vapor pressure, isotherm density, critical point) is scaled by ||(1/\sqrt{n_\mathrm{group}}||), not ||(1/n_\mathrm{group}||) — dividing by n before squaring would let a group's contribution to the sum-of-squares shrink as it grows, hiding a real mismatch behind group size instead of penalizing it. The critical-point term matters beyond its 2 residuals: without it, nothing in the sub-critical VLE objective stops the optimizer from overshooting Tc/p_c while still threading the fitted points. Regularization on the bare-||(D^{*2}||) slots only. c_sigma[3], c_sigma[4], c_epsilon_k[3], c_epsilon_k[4], c_rep[3], c_rep[4] multiply a bare ||(D^{*2}||) term with no ||(C_i(m)||) polynomial prefactor (see the formulas above), unlike [0], [1], [2] of every property. Since ||(D^*||) tops out around 0.05 in the fitted range, ||(D^{*2}||) peaks near 0.0025, so those six coefficients must reach values of order 10-100 just to compete with the well-scaled slots — and a hard bounds=(...) box just gets hit as a wall, wherever it's drawn (tried both (-8, 8) and (-100, 100); both pinned). [0], [1], [2] get no regularization now — they're well-scaled, genuine free parameters exactly like Thijs's (whose fitted values, e.g. c_sigma = [4.15, 17.13, 4.65, ...], are nowhere near a "neutral" 1 — regularizing them toward 1 would only fight the fit). cost appends a small L2 term pulling only the six bare-||(D^{*2}||) slots back toward 0, scaled like the other groups. This lets the fit use them if they earn their keep against real data, but stops the optimizer from trading a large parameter excursion for a marginal cost improvement in what's otherwise a nearly flat direction — an interior optimum instead of a box edge. Low-||(D^*||) anchor for all three properties. The fitted VLE + isotherm data only covers temperatures up to ||(T_c||), i.e. ||(D^* \gtrsim D^*(T_c)||) — below that, nothing constrains c_sigma/c_epsilon_k/c_rep's shape, and (now that [0]/[2] are free too) all three are free to drift arbitrarily far from the literature FH1 curve there, not just c_rep as before. cost adds a residual per property comparing effective_sigma/effective_epsilon_k/effective_rep_ratio under the fitted coefficients against each property's own unfitted curve ([1,1,1,0,0] for ||(\sigma||)/||(\varepsilon||), [1]*5 for ||(\nu||)) at a handful of ||(D^*||) points between 0 and ||(D^*(T_c)||), scaled by ||(1/\sqrt{n}||) like the other groups and an explicit anchor_weight = 0.3 — chosen (for c_rep alone, previously) to noticeably narrow the low-||(D^*||) gap to FH1 without dominating the fit of actual VLE/isotherm data (full 1x weight dragged every data-fit group down with it: cost 0.00077 vs. 0.00021 without any anchor). Raise it for a tighter FH1 match at the cost of fit quality, or lower it to relax back toward the unconstrained fit.
Fitted model vs. baselines
Fitted coefficients

Effective potential parameters vs. quantum parameter ||(D^*||)

||(\sigma_\mathrm{eff}/\sigma||), ||(\varepsilon_\mathrm{eff}/\varepsilon||), and ||(\nu_\mathrm{eff}/\nu||) as functions of ||(D^*||), ported 1:1 from crates/feos/src/uvcs/corresponding_states.rs (effective_sigma/effective_epsilon_k/effective_repulsive_exponent_ratio — same polynomial constants, same rational-function form) so this only re-evaluates the existing Rust formulas in Python rather than approximating them. Compares three curves, all evaluated at the same fixed base rep=8.2761:
  • unfitted (literature FH1): c_scale=1 on every slot that multiplies a genuine ||(C_i(m)||) polynomial, 0 on the slots that only add a bare ||(D^{*2}||) term with no such polynomial — i.e. feos's own default when c_sigma/c_epsilon_k/c_rep are left as None ([1,1,1,0,0] for ||(\sigma||)/||(\varepsilon||), [1,1,1,1,1] for ||(\nu||), since every ||(\nu||) slot has a ||(C_i(m)||) term).
  • Thijs: the baseline ||(uv||)-CS fit's correction coefficients.
  • new Ansatz: this notebook's fitted coefficients.
A vertical line marks ||(D^*(T_c)||): the fitted VLE/isotherm data only spans temperatures up to ||(T_c||), i.e. ||(D^* \gtrsim D^*(T_c) \approx 0.027||) for helium — everything to the left of that line is pure extrapolation with zero data constraining it, which is exactly why cost anchors all three properties there (see the fit section above).
